questions.q: What two required parameters does the nodejs-service template's form collect from the developer?
options: A Docker base image and a Kubernetes namespace
name and owner
A monitoring dashboard URL and an on-call schedule
A GitHub personal access token and a cluster context
questions.explain: The template's parameters block deliberately keeps the form small -- just name and owner -- so there's less for a developer to get wrong.

questions.q: Why does the skeleton's .ci/pipeline.yaml extend Chapter 6's reusable-nodejs-pipeline template instead of defining CI/CD from scratch?
options: So a fix to the shared pipeline template automatically reaches this new service the same way it reaches every other service built from it
Because Backstage templates cannot contain their own pipeline configuration
Because extending a template is required syntax with no functional effect
So the service can skip the scan stage entirely
questions.explain: Extending the shared template keeps this service on the same paved road as everything else, instead of forking its own copy of CI/CD logic.

questions.q: What does the catalog:register scaffolder step actually do?
options: It builds and pushes the service's Docker image
It deletes any existing catalog entry with the same name
It adds the newly published repo to the catalog automatically, using its catalog-info.yaml
It creates the GitHub repository itself
questions.explain: catalog:register is what closes the loop -- the new component becomes visible in the catalog the moment it's created, without a manual follow-up step.

questions.q: Why does the lab check both CI status and the catalog entry separately after running the template, instead of trusting a green pipeline alone?
options: Because a broken catalog:register step can fail silently while publish:github still succeeds, so green CI alone doesn't prove registration worked
Because CI status and catalog data are always identical and the check is redundant
Because Backstage requires two separate logins to view each one
Because the pipeline cannot run until the catalog entry already exists
questions.explain: Green CI only proves the pipeline ran. A resolving catalog entry with the right owner proves the registration half of the golden path worked too, and that half fails silently most often.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Step 3's fs:rename action that seeds the GitOps config repo's overlay directories?
options: It renames the new service's source repository
It deletes the dev environment to save space
It is purely cosmetic and has no effect on deployment
It gives the new service's pipeline somewhere to actually deploy to, matching Chapter 4's directory-per-environment pattern
questions.explain: Without seeded overlay directories, the new service's deploy stage would have nowhere to send a build -- the fourth scaffolder step is what connects it to Chapter 4's existing GitOps structure.
